title: A family isomorphic to a covering is a covering
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site in the sense of Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1): a category with a set $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ of families of morphisms with fixed target such that (i) for every isomorphism $V\to U$ some family $\{V\to U\}$ indexed by a singleton set is a covering, (ii) if $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering and $\{V_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j\in J_i}$ is a covering for every $i$ then $\{V_{ij}\to U\}_{(i,j)}$, indexed by the set of pairs $(i,j)$ with $i\in I$, $j\in J_i$, is a covering, (iii) for a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and a morphism $V\to U$ the fibre products $U_i\times_UV$ exist and, for some choice of them, $\{U_i\times_UV\to V\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering. Let $\{g_a:U_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$ be a covering of $\mathcal C$, and let $\{f_a:V_a\to V\}_{a\in A}$ be a family of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ with common target, indexed by the same set $A$, together with an isomorphism $\varphi:V\to U$ and isomorphisms $\sigma_a:V_a\to U_a$ such that $g_a\circ\sigma_a=\varphi\circ f_a$ for every $a\in A$. Then there are a set $A'$ and a bijection $\beta:A'\to A$ such that $\{f_{\beta(a')}:V_{\beta(a')}\to V\}_{a'\in A'}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. In particular, if $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ is closed under reindexing along bijections of index sets (a family $\{W_j\to W\}_{j\in J}$ is a covering whenever $\{W_{\gamma(k)}\to W\}_{k\in K}$ is one for a bijection $\gamma:K\to J$), then $\{f_a:V_a\to V\}_{a\in A}$ itself is a covering. STATEMENT-DISPUTED (2026-10-10, worker of this item): the earlier conclusion "$\{f_a\}_{a\in A}$ is a covering" without the reindexing does not follow from axioms (i)-(iii) of 00VH, which see the index sets. Counterexample: let $\mathcal C$ have objects $X,Y,U$ and, besides identities, exactly the morphisms $s:X\to Y$, $s^{-1}:Y\to X$, $x:X\to U$, $y:Y\to U$ with $y s=x$ (so $x,y$ are monomorphisms and all fibre products exist). Let $S$ be the smallest set of sets containing $\{\emptyset\}$ and containing $\{(i,j)\}$ (Kuratowski pair) whenever $\{i\},\{j\}\in S$; it is a countable set of singletons. Let $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ be all families $\{h\}_{I}$ of one morphism $h$ indexed by some $I\in S$, except $\{y:Y\to U\}_{\{\emptyset\}}$. (i) holds with index $\{\emptyset\}$ since $y$ is not an isomorphism; (ii) holds since a composite family is indexed by $\{(i,j)\}\neq\{\emptyset\}$; (iii) holds since the only base change that could produce $y$ with index $\{\emptyset\}$ is along $\mathrm{id}_U$, where the fibre product can be chosen as $(X,x)$ or $(U,\mathrm{id}_U)$. Then $\{x\}_{\{\emptyset\}}$ is a covering, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_U$, $\sigma=s^{-1}$ satisfy $x s^{-1}=y$, but $\{y\}_{\{\emptyset\}}$ is not a covering. Mathlib's presieve-based sites (and Stacks' tautological equivalence, Sites 00VU, 00VV, 00VW: tautologically equivalent families have the same sheaf condition) do not see this distinction.

proof.text: *Step 1 (base change along $\varphi$).* Apply axiom (iii) of 00VH [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) to the covering $\{g_a:U_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$ and the morphism $\varphi:V\to U$: the fibre products exist and there is a choice of them, objects $P_a$ with projections $p_a:P_a\to V$, $q_a:P_a\to U_a$, $g_a q_a=\varphi p_a$, each $(P_a,q_a,p_a)$ a fibre product of $g_a$ and $\varphi$, such that $\{p_a:P_a\to V\}_{a\in A}$ is a covering. (This is an instance of the axiom; no claim is made about other choices of fibre products.)

source.place: Definition 00VH (definition-site, line 679), axioms (1)-(3) and the Clarifications paragraph (lines 697-705)

proof.text: *Step 2 ($(V_a,\sigma_a,f_a)$ is a fibre product of $g_a$ and $\varphi$).* We have $g_a\sigma_a=\varphi f_a$. Let $T$ be an object with $u:T\to U_a$, $v:T\to V$, $g_a u=\varphi v$. A morphism $t:T\to V_a$ with $\sigma_a t=u$ must be $t=\sigma_a^{-1}u$, so there is at most one $t$ with $\sigma_a t=u$, $f_a t=v$. For $t=\sigma_a^{-1}u$: $\sigma_a t=u$, and $\varphi f_a t=g_a\sigma_a t=g_a u=\varphi v$, hence $f_a t=v$ since $\varphi$ is an isomorphism (compose with $\varphi^{-1}$). So $t$ exists and is unique: $(V_a,\sigma_a,f_a)$ is a fibre product $U_a\times_UV$.

source.place: definition of fibre product (Categories, Section 001U, Definition 001V); argument written out by the worker

proof.text: *Step 3 (comparison isomorphisms).* By Steps 1 and 2, $(P_a,q_a,p_a)$ and $(V_a,\sigma_a,f_a)$ are both fibre products of $g_a$ and $\varphi$. By the universal property of $P_a$ there is a unique $\tau_a:V_a\to P_a$ with $q_a\tau_a=\sigma_a$ and $p_a\tau_a=f_a$, and by that of $V_a$ a unique $\rho_a:P_a\to V_a$ with $\sigma_a\rho_a=q_a$, $f_a\rho_a=p_a$; then $\rho_a\tau_a$ and $\mathrm{id}_{V_a}$ both satisfy the conditions defining the factorization of $(\sigma_a,f_a)$ through $V_a$, so $\rho_a\tau_a=\mathrm{id}$, and likewise $\tau_a\rho_a=\mathrm{id}$. So $\tau_a$ is an isomorphism with $p_a\tau_a=f_a$.

source.place: uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism (Categories, Section 001U, Definition 001V); argument written out by the worker

proof.text: *Step 4 (composition).* By axiom (i) [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), for each $a\in A$ there is a singleton set $J_a=\{j_a\}$ such that $\{\tau_a:V_a\to P_a\}_{j\in J_a}$ is a covering (Step 3: $\tau_a$ is an isomorphism). By axiom (ii) applied to the covering $\{p_a\}_{a\in A}$ of Step 1 and these coverings, the family $\{p_a\tau_a:V_a\to V\}_{(a,j)\in A'}$, $A'=\{(a,j_a):a\in A\}$, is a covering. By Step 3, $p_a\tau_a=f_a$.

source.place: Definition 00VH (definition-site, line 679), axioms (1)-(3) and the Clarifications paragraph (lines 697-705)

proof.text: *Step 5 (conclusion).* The map $\beta:A'\to A$, $(a,j_a)\mapsto a$, is a bijection (inverse $a\mapsto(a,j_a)$), and by Step 4 $\{f_{\beta(a')}:V_{\beta(a')}\to V\}_{a'\in A'}$ is a covering. If $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$ is closed under reindexing along bijections, applying this with $\gamma=\beta$ shows that $\{f_a\}_{a\in A}$ is a covering. (Without that hypothesis the conclusion with index set $A$ can fail; see the counterexample in the statement.)

The worker is right that 00VH sees index sets; the lead added to def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology (1) the convention that coverings are closed under bijective reindexing (true for every site of this document, Sites 00VU/00VX for the general case), under which the "in particular" clause gives the family indexed by A itself, as used by lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-morphism-transport Step 4(a). split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks Sites 00VH and its Clarifications. The statement as written was false: the axioms see index sets (axiom (1) gives a covering indexed by some singleton, axiom (2) gives a family indexed by pairs), and a site can contain a covering {x}_{\{0\}} while the isomorphic family {y}_{\{0\}} is not a covering (counterexample now in the statement, marked STATEMENT-DISPUTED). Corrected the conclusion to: a reindexing of {f_a} along a bijection A'->A is a covering, and {f_a}_{a in A} itself is one if Cov is closed under bijective reindexing. Proof in 5 steps from axioms (iii), (i), (ii) and the universal property of fibre products (all elementary or instances of the axioms of the definition node). The Clarifications paragraph does not say that (iii) holds for every choice of fibre products; that is avoided here by comparing the chosen fibre product with V_a directly. No new nodes. Mathlib re-searched with three kinds: no match (Mathlib's presieve-based precoverages have no index sets).
